purpose: Tafasitamab-cxix is used to treat a type of blood cancer called diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) in adults whose cancer has come back or did not respond to previous treatment. It is used together with another medicine called lenalidomide. It is meant for patients who are not able to receive a stem cell transplant.
how_it_works: Your immune system has special proteins called antibodies that help fight harmful cells. Tafasitamab-cxix is a man-made antibody that targets a specific protein called CD19 found on the surface of certain cancer cells. Once it attaches to the cancer cell, it signals your immune system to destroy it and can also directly kill the cancer cell.
common_side_effects: Feeling very tired or weak, low blood cell counts (which can increase risk of infection or bleeding), nausea, diarrhea, swelling in the arms or legs, decreased appetite, fever, and rash. Some people may also notice cough or shortness of breath.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious drops in blood cell counts, which increases your risk of serious infections and bleeding — your doctor will monitor your blood regularly. It can cause serious allergic or infusion reactions during or after your IV treatment, so tell your nurse right away if you feel chills, fever, flushing, or trouble breathing. It may harm an unborn baby, so both men and women must use effective birth control during and after treatment. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an IV infusion (through a vein) by a healthcare provider, not at home. It is typically given once a week for the first two cycles (about 28 days each), then once every two weeks after that. Your doctor will decide the exact schedule and dose based on your specific situation and how well you tolerate the treatment.
